metadata.title: Pedagogical practices and civic knowledge and engagement in Latin America: Multilevel analysis using ICCS data

confounders_identified: Highest level of education the student expects to achieve (S_ISCED)
Interest of the student in political and social issues (S_SINT)
Frequency with which the student discusses or talks about political or social issues outside of school (S_POLDISC)
extraction.outcome_summary: The study analyzed ICCS 2016 data from five Latin American countries (Chile, Colombia, the Dominican Republic, Mexico, and Peru) using hierarchical linear models with weighted multilevel estimation. It found that civic learning in school, openness in classroom discussions, and some forms of civic participation were significantly associated with civic knowledge, but the direction and magnitude of associations varied by country. Across countries, expected electoral participation was positively related to civic knowledge, whereas expected active political participation was consistently negative. Girls, higher educational aspirations, and home literacy resources were also associated with higher civic knowledge in most countries.
